verdict.rationale: Snyk documents natural-language operation through its local MCP server: you prompt your coding agent with phrases like "scan my directory for security issues" (snyk-docs-11, snyk-docs-28, snyk-docs-35). It also offers slash commands such as /snyk-fix and /snyk-batch-fix, and an LLM-driven Remediation Agent inside coding assistants or via `snyk fix --agentic` (snyk-docs-12, snyk-docs-13, snyk-docs-23). However, natural-language control depends on a third-party agentic development environment rather than a native conversational interface, and the documented examples cover mainly scanning and fixing. missing for 10: a first-party natural-language interface in the Snyk platform or UI, natural-language coverage beyond scan/fix (e.g. policy, reporting, admin), independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language commands work reliably.
